record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: Is the cosmic microwave background radiation necessarily a relic of a high-energy primordial universe, or can an astrophysical or static-universe scenario explain its observed temperature, nearly blackbody spectrum, isotropy, and thermalization without requiring an opaque universe that conflicts with the observed transparency to high-redshift radio galaxies?

evidence.quote: Anyway, the radiation is there and the question is the origin of this radiation not the discoverer. Is the high energy primordial Universe the only possible scenario?
The mechanism of thermalization in any of these cases is perhaps the hardest problem.
At present there is not a satisfactory alternative scenario which has no problem to explain the Microwave Background Radiation, so the standard scenario seems the best solution.

artifact.status_search_result: No alternative (non–hot Big Bang) model has been demonstrated to satisfy all the listed observational constraints simultaneously; reviews and precision CMB measurements (COBE/FIRAS, WMAP, Planck) continue to support the relic interpretation, while proposed astrophysical thermalization scenarios face severe difficulties with the blackbody spectrum and with universe transparency to high-redshift radio sources. The question of a viable consistent alternative therefore remains open in the sense that no such model has been established, although the standard hot Big Bang scenario is widely regarded as the only currently satisfactory explanation.

status_evidence.title: FIRAS measurements of the CMB blackbody spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: COBE/FIRAS measured the CMB spectrum to be a near-perfect blackbody at T = 2.725 K with deviations smaller than 50 parts per million.
status_evidence.claim: Precision blackbody spectrum is a tight observational constraint that any alternative thermalization model must reproduce.
